title: IMED in flow-lenia: food-eating Flow-Lenia gliders divide (generation 4-6), and when one fresh daughter's food is cut it dissolves within 130-260 t while its sister glides on and divides and its fed twin grows (6/6 seeds)
summary: fl_forager's matter is made only from a conserved, diffusing food field. In a labkit pack (3 seeds, t=800) one noise patch gives 10-14 crescent gliders that travel 7-11.5 body lengths and divide to generation 4-6 (merge/split 0.72-0.82). At a fresh division (daughters 18-26 px apart) I branched a fed twin and a run in which a food-cut disk follows one daughter. On 6/6 seeds the starved daughter stops, shrinks and dissolves by 130-260 t after the fork, much faster than decay, while its sister glides on, grows 1.9-6x and divides, and the same daughter in the fed twin grows and divides. A passive shell channel S (r-two56's set-point ring) outlines each glider but is a readout and is not claimed.

claims.statement: In world.py, the crescent gliders that grow out of one noise patch glide 7-11.5 body lengths and divide to generation 4-6 (pack seeds 0-2); at a fresh division, the daughter whose food is cut dissolves within 130-260 t while its sister glides and divides, and in the fed twin the same daughter grows and divides (forks seeds 0-5).
claims.track: seed 3 (forks/df3.png): two daughters of a division 18 px apart at t=190, each gliding; in the fed twin the + daughter glides, grows from mass 50 to 90 and divides again; in the cut run it stops and dissolves by t=368 while the x sister glides, grows to 6x and divides

controls_run.E: forks/df<0-5>.png and forks/dfork_summary.json: fed twin from the identical fork state, food cut following one daughter, 6 seeds
